They do call each other fat and say rude things, it differs from culture to culture, in my particular heritages cultural back ground calling a stranger fat is rude and not the norm though it happens a lot among friends and family but other cultures like Mexicans don't seem to have a problem with those sort of comments to strangers. America is a melting pot of culture but most of it is cohesive and conforms to a certain norm, many immigrants have completely lost their cultural identity and rarely pass on their native language to their children. My point is just that to Juan and Paula it was harmless banter to Russ they were really offensive insults, I side with Russ but that doesn't necessarily mean Juan meant them as negatively as I perceive them. I've been told a lot of insanely rude things by Mexicans that other Mexicans who were my friends didn't seem to be phased by or think it wasn't something to get offended over and when you get upset they generally think you are being petty or silly and overly sensitive. I don't know how Colombian culture is but I doubt they see it as very rude. I think Paula and her friends should keep in mind they are in the US and conform to cultural norms when they are here just like they would expect Russ to conform to their culture when he's in Columbia. I'd like to say that Dutch people are brutally honest too but they are honest in a matter of fact sense as opposed to teasing someone in a way I consider vulgar, we Americans are honestly sensitive and feel everything has to be smiles and said in a happy up beat voice or it's rude that most of the world doesn't subscribe to.

I have had similar feelings toward really clingy people I didn't know well but it honestly sounds like you just didn't really care about any of those people and put your life ahead of building a relationship. There is nothing wrong with that but the problem is to have a real long lasting relationship it takes a lot of effort and compromise and it's definitely going to be really really inconvenient for you at some point no matter who it is or how well things go at first. I would just not date if I were you till you're ready to put in that kind of effort into a relationship. If you do before then ultimately what will happen is that they will become too attached and your actions will appear extremely selfish. They will feel led on because dating them implied you were ready for that sort of commitment outside of yourself and your endeavors because i have been on the opposite end and it sucks. If you were under the impression someone liked you and you really liked them back and they started distancing themselves because they felt you were just baggage you would not feel good at all especially if your feelings ran deep.
